While you tried to contact him for two weeks, selling someone else’s property for personal profit without following legal procedures is ethically and legally wrong. - **Legal Perspective:** Even if the roommate abandoned the items, most jurisdictions require specific steps before disposal/sale (e.g., sending formal notice, waiting a set period, selling at auction and remitting proceeds minus costs to the owner). Selling directly to a store and pocketing the cash bypasses these requirements and constitutes conversion (theft of property). - **Ethical Perspective:** The games weren’t yours to sell. Your responsibility was to either (a) dispose of them properly (e.g., trash) to avoid deposit deductions, or (b) follow legal protocols for abandoned property and return any proceeds to the roommate. Selling for profit was never the right move. **Bottom line:** You acted out of self-interest, not responsibility. Return the money or offer to split it with him—this isn’t a “he left it behind, so it’s mine” situation.
